writing.abstract_text: Peak-position limits concern the largest absolute inventory reached before a review ends, making completed path labels and the observed current position central to forecasting. We compare historical and conditional quantile reports for an FX market maker and weekly primary-dealer position aggregates, using matched histories and update schedules. Simple historical rules remain demanding benchmarks across frequencies, position categories and reference choices. At the shorter horizon, long-history FX regression lowers matched loss by 14.8% and 16.6% in the previously reported later and earlier windows. A post hoc history-to-horizon coordinate organizes simulation gains, and a new simulation passes its short-history and long-history prediction screens. Real-record learning curves partly support the predicted first cutpoints, while left censoring, large-history reversals and failures of universal simplification qualify that pattern. For limit managers, these findings motivate matching historical information before assessing conditional forecasts jointly on score, breaches and stability, with history length guiding evaluation.
